subject: ss-radiology
title: Diffuse lung disease and HRCT: pattern recognition for the key ILDs

steps.tx: A patient with worsening breathlessness on exertion, fine crackles at the lung bases and no fever should raise suspicion of **interstitial lung disease** (ILD). This umbrella term covers well over two hundred varied disorders. Although the **interstitium** is the main target, damage to alveolar lining cells and vessel-lining cells also fuels fibrosis. Hearing **egophony** or **bronchial breathing** tends to point toward airspace filling, such as infection, rather than scarring. A **high-resolution CT** scan is now the first-line imaging test and may establish a **usual interstitial pneumonia** pattern without needing biopsy.
steps.say: A patient with worsening breathlessness on exertion, fine crackles at the lung bases and no fever should raise suspicion of interstitial lung disease. This umbrella term covers well over two hundred varied disorders. Although the interstitium is the main target, damage to alveolar lining cells and vessel-lining cells also fuels fibrosis. Hearing egophony or bronchial breathing tends to point toward airspace filling, such as infection, rather than scarring. A high-resolution CT scan is now the first-line imaging test and may establish a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern without needing biopsy.

steps.tx: Interstitial lung diseases can first be sorted by whether a trigger is identified. **Known-cause** groups include occupational dust, medications, connective tissue disorders and granulomatous conditions such as **hypersensitivity pneumonitis**. When no trigger is found, the disease is labelled **unknown-cause**, and the **idiopathic interstitial pneumonias** make up the largest share. Consensus classification then places these into chronic fibrosing, smoking-related and acute or subacute patterns.
steps.say: Start by asking whether a cause can be identified. Known-cause groups include occupational dust, drugs, connective tissue disease and granulomatous disease such as hypersensitivity pneumonitis. If no trigger is found, the disease is unknown-cause, and the idiopathic interstitial pneumonias form the largest share. Under the consensus scheme these split into chronic fibrosing, smoking-related and acute or subacute groups. Rarer unknown-cause entities, including lymphangioleiomyomatosis, alveolar proteinosis, Langerhans cell histiocytosis and sarcoidosis, sit alongside them.

steps.tx: **Hypersensitivity pneumonitis** (HP) is an immune reaction to inhaled antigens that reach distal airways and alveoli. It is now classified as nonfibrotic or fibrotic rather than acute, subacute or chronic. Chronic fibrotic HP can mirror IPF on imaging. Sarcoidosis shows hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy with peribronchovascular nodularity, and its nodules follow a perilymphatic distribution. Eosinophilia above 25% on BAL suggests chronic eosinophilic pneumonia.
steps.say: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is an immune reaction to inhaled antigens that reach the distal airways and alveoli. It is now classified as nonfibrotic or fibrotic. Chronic fibrotic HP can mirror IPF on imaging. Sarcoidosis shows hilar and mediastinal lymphadenopathy with peribronchovascular nodularity, with nodules following a perilymphatic distribution. Eosinophilia above 25 percent on bronchoalveolar lavage suggests chronic eosinophilic pneumonia.

steps.tx: For management, HRCT, **transfer factor** (DLCO) and FVC form the core work-up, plus connective tissue and exposure screening. Severity depends on fibrosis extent, PFT decline and pulmonary hypertension. Refer progressive, treatment-refractory disease to a multidisciplinary ILD team and consider lung transplantation. Surgical lung biopsy is reserved for cases still unclear after multidisciplinary review. Acute exacerbations of fibrotic ILD carry mortality above 85 percent.
